analysis:
The only changed lines in ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift sit in unloadModel. The Nemotron Super retirement path at base 1151 now calls selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now: .now) when retirement succeeds. The general unload path at head ~1222 makes the same call after retryReserveDeferredPrefetches. I treated this as a scheduling change: it marks waiting selected models as due for the next capacity tick. It adds no data path, cryptography, authorization, attestation, prompt handling, key handling or cache-storage change, so T-041 (prefix cache/SSD) and the load-gate logic do not appear to be affected.

The rest of the supplied model-load flow (weight-hash bracketing, add-on hold refusal, KV headroom guards, reslice gate) is unchanged context. I confirmed it does not interact with the new calls. The new calls run after the slot, weights and grants are released. There is no new lock-ordering issue in the supplied evidence, and the gate is not held at that point.

Residual question, outside the supplied evidence: selectedModelRecovery's implementation (makeAllDue and the capacity tick that consumes it) is not shown. Its loads should still pass the same ensureModelLoaded admission, including the add-on hold refusal (TB-012/T-059), the memory gate and the weight-hash verification. If makeAllDue triggers loads that bypass those checks, or loops without backoff, that would be an availability concern (T-059/T-060 class), but there is no evidence of either. The unload paths are also reachable via eviction, so a reload/evict churn loop is a theoretical availability concern that depends on the recovery code, which I did not see.
